- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a 3–5 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 2–5% for the first 3 days.
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; lag the forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment changes abruptly.
- Mean reversion is stronger in the 10–15 day horizon; if forecast deviates >3σ from recent 10-day average, revert toward that average.
- In bullish sentiment, model often forecasts higher than true outcome in the 20–30 day horizon; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 10-day high for safety.
